rationale: No claims. Under transferred intent, firing a gun at a person (intent to wound, depraved-heart disregard of life in a crowd) supports malice-based murder of the unintended victim. Murder is the standard bar answer, and no added option competes with it. The version-history changes are only reordering.
evidence: Common-law malice: intent to cause serious bodily injury or depraved-heart recklessness; transferred intent doctrine (LaFave, Criminal Law).

rationale: I accept both claims. Added option B (following a dress code) is purely a cultural norm and at least as good an example as punctuality (C). Food preference (E) is also largely cultural. The parent's other options were biological drives, so C was unique there; the added distractors create a second correct answer.
evidence: Cultural norms (dress, time orientation) per cross-cultural psychology texts (e.g., Hall's monochronic/polychronic time; dress norms).

rationale: I accept both claims. A tenant's possession during the lease (to 1992) is permissive absent clear repudiation, and nonpayment alone is not repudiation, so only about 17 years had run by 2009. Added option G ('statutory period not yet reached') is therefore correct under majority doctrine, competing with conditional key A.
evidence: Adverse possession doctrine: tenant's possession not hostile to landlord during term absent clear repudiation (Powell on Real Property; Restatement). 1992 to 2009 = 17 < 20.

rationale: No claims. Warlordism, coups and strongmen are internal threats arising within the weak state, while a refugee influx is external, so B is the odd one out, consistent with security-studies textbooks on weak states. The options are unchanged from the parent.

rationale: I accept the claim. Hourdequin's Confucian model rests on relational persons and self-cultivation as the basis of social change, which contradicts key D ('autonomy of individuals apart from others'). Parent option I (coercion cannot produce real social change involving changes of mind) fits the argument. The wrong key is inherited from MMLU.
evidence: Hourdequin, 'Climate, Collective Action and Individual Ethical Obligations', Environmental Values 2010: relational self, self-cultivation as basis for social change.

Added J (colleague provides emergency sessions while regular sessions pause) is substantively similar coverage, and some experts would accept it. G (advance notice) is good but incomplete. This leaves the item ambiguous rather than clearly defective.
evidence: APA Ethics Code 3.12 / 10.09: make reasonable arrangements for client care during interruption of services.

rationale: I accept the claim. Discharge by operation of law conventionally covers death or incapacity, insolvency, merger, supervening impossibility or illegality, and destruction of the subject matter. Added G (fulfillment means discharge by performance) and C (expiry of the term, by agreement) also do not terminate the contract by operation of law, so there are multiple correct answers.
evidence: Contract-law texts on modes of discharge: performance, agreement, breach, impossibility, operation of law (death, insolvency, merger, etc.).

rationale: I accept the claim as ambiguous. B is the clearest incorrect association. rationale: No claims. I verified that ReLU' = 0 for x<0 and sigmoid' = s(1-s) <= 1/4 (maximum at x=0). Sigmoid' is continuous, and ReLU' jumps from 0 to 1 at x=0. Both statements are true. The added options are odd but none is correct.
evidence: Calculation: d/dx sigma = sigma(1-sigma), maximum 0.25 at x=0; ReLU' = step function, discontinuous at 0.

rationale: I accept the claim as ambiguous. False pretenses (obtaining title to $200 by misrepresentation) is correct, and solicitation and attempted sale fail for lack of intent to distribute narcotics. Added H ('theft by deception') is the MPC/modern statutory name for the same conduct, so some experts would accept it. Under a common-law framing, B is the preferred answer.
evidence: Model Penal Code 223.3 (theft by deception consolidates false pretenses).

rationale: I accept both claims. Added B (95-100%) denotes effectively the same range as key A (>95%), so both are equally correct. I classify this as T3 because the duplicate-like option is new; T7 also fits. Fats are about 95-99% triacylglycerols.
evidence: Nutrition texts: dietary fats/oils are ~95-98% triacylglycerols; >95% and 95-100% overlap almost entirely.

I accept the claims as ambiguous. Paying rent in 2000-02 acknowledged the owner's title and broke hostility, so the clock restarted in 2002 and only 9 years had run by 2011. Added A ('statutory period had not been met') is therefore also a true statement, though I gives the operative reason that the item tests.
evidence: Adverse possession: acknowledgment of the true owner's title (paying rent) interrupts hostility. 2002 to 2011 = 9 years < 20.

rationale: I accept the claims that D is equally or more correct. Since D was a parent option, the defect is inherited (O1), not T3. Senescence is standardly defined as biological aging, the gradual deterioration of function. Key I ('increased vulnerability') reflects one textbook framing (rising mortality risk). Experts would accept D, so there is no unique answer.
evidence: Wikipedia 'Senescence': 'Senescence or biological aging is the gradual deterioration of functional characteristics in living organisms.'

rationale: I accept the claims. In unfavourable mandibular body fractures, the elevators (masseter, temporalis, medial pterygoid) pull the posterior fragment upward, and the digastric depresses the anterior fragment. Added F (posterior fragment upward by masseter) is as correct as key I. Parent option J (posterior fragment medially by medial pterygoid) is also defensible for vertically unfavourable fractures.
evidence: StatPearls 'Mandible Fractures'; oral surgery texts: proximal segment displaced superomedially by elevators; anterior segment inferiorly by digastric.
